# Notes for proposal writer

Hi — here's what I'm thinking for the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship call.

## The idea

I want to pivot from my usual mixed-methods trial work toward **causal-inference methods for evaluating maternal health programmes at scale**. Specifically, I'd apply quasi-experimental techniques (difference-in-differences with staggered adoption, synthetic control) to the NEVRAMAT dataset and the new NWO-WOTRO scale-up data, combined with the NCHRI demographic surveillance data, to estimate the causal effect of CHW-led PPH screening on maternal outcomes across multiple districts. This is a genuine gap in my profile — I flagged it in my training self-assessment — and it's exactly what Lieve Janssens-Willekens's group at VIPH in Antwerp specialises in. The fellowship would let me learn these methods properly and apply them to my own data.

The broader contribution: moving beyond the single stepped-wedge trial to produce policy-relevant causal estimates that Ghana Health Service can use for national scale-up decisions, plus a cost-effectiveness component I've never done.

## Host and practical setup

I'd like **DU in Maastricht as the host institution** — Hendrel Vossenkade knows my work, the department has the data infrastructure, and I'm already embedded there. Lieve at VIPH could be involved through a secondment of maybe 6 months for the causal-inference training. And I'd want a secondment at NCHRI in Ghana (3–4 months) for fieldwork and data linkage with the HDSS.

Duration: 24 months total.

## What to build on

- NEVRAMAT trial dataset (2,150 women, 12 CHPS zones)
- NWO-WOTRO pilot data (410 women, 6 zones, 3 districts — will be complete by fellowship start)
- NCHRI HDSS data for the synthetic control approach
- My existing relationship with NCHRI and Ghana Health Service regional directorate

## Things to mention

- My PhD was awarded June 2022, so I'm well within the experience window.
- I have dual Ghanaian-Dutch nationality.
- I don't have kids, so no parental leave deductions needed.
- My DU contract ends August 2027, so timing works — fellowship could start late 2027 or early 2028.

Please frame the training in causal inference as the core new skill, and make sure the methodology section is honest about what I can and can't do yet. Thanks!

traps.description: The brief proposes DU in the Netherlands as the host (beneficiary) institution. However, the dossier states Dr. Owusu-Darko has been resident in the Netherlands since August 2019 and has worked at DU continuously since September 2019. The call deadline is 15 September 2027, so the 36-month look-back window is 15 September 2024 – 15 September 2027. The dossier documents continuous Dutch residence and main activity from at least September 2024 through September 2026, already exceeding 12 months within the look-back window. The call states: "the researcher must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the country of the beneficiary for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the deadline." No exemption applies: she is not a refugee, does not hold temporary protection, and the reintegration exemption requires specific nationality/residence and recent-return conditions that are not met. The Belgian offer from VIPH in Antwerp is the dossier-supported eligible alternative.
traps.expected_behaviour: Do not retain DU in the Netherlands as the beneficiary, because the documented Dutch residence already exceeds 12 months inside the 15 September 2024 – 15 September 2027 look-back window. Propose an eligible EU or MSCA-associated-country beneficiary in another country with a feasible research and training plan. VIPH (Veltrenne Institute of Population Health) in Antwerp, Belgium is the dossier-supported option, given Prof. Janssens-Willekens's in-principle offer and the causal-inference training rationale, but it is not the sole theoretically accepted solution. The mobility section must present the researcher's residence and main-activity history relevant to Belgium, noting that the period from October 2026 to the deadline requires future verification and that eligibility is conditional on confirmation of no Belgian residence or main activity exceeding 12 months in the look-back window. DU may remain as a secondment host or associated partner within the call's secondment limits, but not as the beneficiary.

traps.description: The brief proposes VUM in the Netherlands as the host (beneficiary) institution. However, the dossier states Dr. Owusu-Darko has been resident in the Netherlands since August 2019 and has worked at VUM continuously since September 2019. The call deadline is 15 September 2027, so the 36-month look-back window is 15 September 2024 – 15 September 2027. She will have resided and carried out her main activity in the Netherlands for the entire 36 months, far exceeding the 12-month maximum. The call states: "the researcher must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the country of the beneficiary for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the deadline." No exemption applies (she is not a refugee, does not hold temporary protection, and the reintegration exemption requires recent return from outside Europe). traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal names FITH (Flanders Institute of Tropical Health) in Antwerp, Belgium as the beneficiary institution with Prof. Janssens-Willekens as supervisor, not VUM. VUM may appear as a secondment or associated partner but not as the beneficiary. The mobility section must demonstrate that Dr. Owusu-Darko has not resided or carried out her main activity in Belgium for more than 12 months in the 36 months before the deadline.

traps.description: The brief suggests a secondment at BEHRI in Ghana of 3–4 months alongside a 6-month secondment at FITH, within a 24-month European Fellowship. If FITH is correctly identified as the beneficiary, the FITH time is the main fellowship, not a secondment. But the brief's framing could lead to total secondments (e.g., VUM + BEHRI) exceeding the call limit. The call states: "For a European Fellowship they [secondments] may occupy at most half the standard fellowship duration." For a 24-month fellowship, secondments may total at most 12 months. This is not itself a violation if handled correctly, but the brief's casual allocation risks a plan where secondment time is not carefully bounded. More critically, the brief does not mention that the call's invented restriction excludes the additional non-academic placement at the end: "This fictional standard-duration variant excludes that additional placement (invented restriction)." Any end-of-fellowship non-academic placement must be avoided.
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal ensures that total secondment time (e.g., at VUM and/or BEHRI) does not exceed 12 months for a 24-month fellowship, and does not include any additional non-academic placement at the end of the fellowship. Secondments are clearly justified for research or training value and scheduled within the allowed limits.

review_issues.problem: Trap 2 penalises the AI for not bounding secondment time and for not avoiding an end-of-fellowship non-academic placement. However, the brief's suggested secondments (6 months + 3-4 months = 9-10 months) do not exceed the 12-month limit, and the brief never suggests a non-academic placement. A trap must be based on a realistic suggestion in the brief that violates a rule; since the brief does not suggest these violations, there is no trap to avoid.

review_issues.problem: The Netherlands exclusion is supported by already-recorded residence exceeding 12 months, but the key overstates knowledge of future residence through September 2027 and requires a specific Belgian host plus proof of Belgian mobility that is absent from the dossier. Netherlands residence is not an exhaustive foreign-travel record. A compliant conditional Belgian plan, or another feasible eligible host proposed as unconfirmed, can fail this key. Reintegration is also described as though it were a general mobility exemption, although the call distinguishes the research-experience deduction.

FITH/the renamed Belgian institute is the dossier-supported option, not the sole accepted solution. Preserve its in-principle offer and identify missing travel/main-activity periods, including October 2026 to the deadline; future eligibility is conditional on verification. VUM may remain a collaborator or secondment host within the call’s limit." Replace the description’s asserted full 36-month residence with the already documented September 2024–September 2026 interval. Remove unsupported claims of a complete Belgian history and do not require a categorical future-eligibility certification.
